observations.fact: /scratch skill SKILL.md lines 97-101 explicitly state: 'Files in scratch are DELETED by the SessionEnd hook (harvest-session.sh). Non-ephemeral .md files are copied to harvesting/ with a date prefix before deletion. All other files are deleted without backup.'

/scratch skill SKILL.md lines 103-107 explicitly state: 'Never put carry-forward artifacts in scratch. Handoff prompts, planning briefs, running estimates, and any artifact that must survive the session MUST be written to a permanent tracked location.' Running estimates are called out BY NAME.

harvest-session.sh lines 73-79 classify .json files: config/lock patterns (package-lock*, node_modules*, *.config.json, tsconfig*) are ephemeral; ALL OTHER .json files are marked as artifacts (is_ephemeral=false). A file named running-estimate.json does NOT match any ephemeral pattern.

harvest-session.sh lines 96-161: non-ephemeral files are COPIED (not moved) to harvesting/ with a date prefix (e.g., 2026-03-21_running-estimate.json) IF the project has a harvesting/ directory. If no harvesting/ directory exists, non-ephemeral files are treated as ephemeral (deleted).

harvest-session.sh lines 164-166: AFTER classification and harvesting, the entire session directory is deleted via 'rm -rf $SESSION_DIR'. The file is gone from scratch regardless of whether it was harvested.

The harvest manifest (harvesting/harvest-manifest.json) contains 60 harvested artifacts spanning 7 sessions. ZERO are .json files. All are .md, .py, .sh, .pl, or .ps1. This means the .json harvest path has never been exercised in production.

The aitools-workspace rule (.claude/rules/aitools-workspace.md line 39) defines running-estimate.json as belonging at .aitools/channel/running-estimate.json with 'tracked' status. This is the CANONICAL location for running estimates.

.gitignore line 47 blanket-ignores '.aitools/' — this means .aitools/channel/running-estimate.json is gitignored despite the workspace rule declaring it as 'tracked'. The workspace rule and the gitignore CONTRADICT each other.

There is a LIVE running-estimate.json in the current session's scratch directory (.scratch/session-5HyCwPtSDH/running-estimate.json, 13.8 KB). This is the exact anti-pattern the /scratch skill warns against on lines 103-107.

There is also a running estimate at .aitools/channel/session-uyZ7TELqpP/20260316T190000Z_s3_running-estimate.json from a March 16 session. This file is in the gitignored .aitools/ directory, meaning it exists only on this one machine.

tool-ops.json has a 'mock-json-pipe' verification pattern for hook testing (tool-ops.json lines 49-66). This pattern pipes JSON to a hook script and checks exit code + stdout regex. It could be adapted to test harvest-session.sh classification behavior, but currently only covers the deny-rule hook.

The /handoff skill SKILL.md lines 313-316 explicitly states: 'The handoff MUST be written to a PERMANENT tracked location -- never to session scratch. Scratch directories are deleted by the SessionEnd hook (harvest-session.sh lines 164-166).' AND lines 527-533 state: 'Files in .scratch/ are deleted by the SessionEnd hook. Handoffs, carry-forward state, and any artifact that must persist MUST be written to a permanent tracked location.'

The harvest-session.sh manifest update (lines 126-154) sets type='code' for ALL harvested artifacts, regardless of actual content. A running-estimate.json would be harvested as type='code' with language=null (json is not in the langMap). The 'description' is always 'Auto-harvested from session scratch'.

The aitools-workspace rule line 27 states: 'Session-ephemeral data (scratch files, in-flight channel messages) is gitignored -- it belongs to one session on one machine.' But the running estimate is NOT session-ephemeral -- it is carry-forward state per the same rule line 22.

scratch-init.sh lines 30-34: stale session dirs (>24h) are cleaned up at session start. If a session crashes and SessionEnd never fires, the next session's SessionStart hook will rm -rf any session dir older than 24 hours. A running estimate in scratch from a crashed session would be silently destroyed with no harvesting.

insights.analysis: A running-estimate.json in scratch would be HARVESTED, not deleted — but only if the project has a harvesting/ directory. The classification logic on lines 73-79 treats generic .json as non-ephemeral. It would be copied to harvesting/2026-03-21_running-estimate.json, entered in the manifest as type='code'/language=null, and then the original would be rm -rf'd with the session dir. The S3 agent's assumption ('deleted at session end') was partially wrong: the file is copied before deletion. But the original M1's deeper finding is correct: 'harvested != carry-forward'. The harvested copy sits in harvesting/ with a 30-day prune timer, not in the canonical .aitools/channel/ location, not tracked in git (harvesting/ IS tracked but the carry-forward semantics are wrong — it becomes an artifact to evaluate, not operational state to continue from).

The canonical location for running estimates (.aitools/channel/running-estimate.json) is currently BROKEN. The workspace rule says it should be 'tracked' (in git), but .gitignore blanket-ignores .aitools/. This means even if an agent writes to the correct canonical location, the file will never be committed, never survive a machine switch, and never achieve its carry-forward purpose. The March 16 running estimate at .aitools/channel/session-uyZ7TELqpP/ confirms this: it exists on this machine only. This is finding F1 from the running estimate itself.

The /scratch skill and /handoff skill both explicitly call out running estimates as things that MUST NOT go in scratch. The /scratch skill names 'running estimates' by name in its prohibition. Yet the current session has a 13.8 KB running-estimate.json sitting in .scratch/session-5HyCwPtSDH/. This means either: (a) the agent that wrote it did not read the /scratch skill, (b) the agent read it but did not have a working canonical location to write to (because .aitools/ is gitignored), or (c) both. The most likely explanation is (b) — the workspace rule says the canonical location is .aitools/channel/, but that is gitignored, so agents fall back to scratch because it at least exists.

The .json harvesting path in harvest-session.sh has NEVER been exercised in production. Zero of 60 harvested artifacts are .json files. This means the classification logic for .json (lines 73-79), the manifest entry format (type='code', language=null), and the pruning behavior for .json artifacts are all untested code paths. If a running-estimate.json were the first .json to be harvested, it would be classified as 'code' — which is semantically wrong (it is operational state, not code). The auto-harvest description would be generic ('Auto-harvested from session scratch'), losing the context that this was a running estimate.

There are TWO deletion paths for scratch files, and only one involves harvesting. The SessionEnd hook (harvest-session.sh) classifies, harvests, then deletes. But the SessionStart hook (scratch-init.sh) has a stale-dir cleanup that rm -rfs any session dir older than 24 hours WITHOUT harvesting. If a session crashes (SessionEnd never fires) and the user starts a new session more than 24 hours later, everything in that crashed session's scratch dir — including any running estimates, research docs, or code — is silently destroyed. This is a silent data-loss path for any non-committed state in scratch.

The tool-ops mock-json-pipe verification pattern could be adapted to test harvest-session.sh classification. You would pipe a mock SessionEnd payload with a session dir containing various file types, then verify which files appear in harvesting/ and which are deleted. However, this would require: (1) creating a temp session dir with test files, (2) running harvest-session.sh against it, (3) checking the harvesting/ dir for expected artifacts. The existing pattern only covers stdin-to-stdout hook testing. A lifecycle test would be a new verification type (e.g., 'mock-session-lifecycle').

The harness has THREE authoritative sources that all agree running estimates belong in a permanent tracked location, yet provides no working implementation of that location. The /scratch skill says 'never put carry-forward artifacts in scratch', the workspace rule says '.aitools/channel/running-estimate.json tracked', and the cross-machine carry-forward principle says 'if data needs to survive a machine switch, it must be tracked'. All three agree. But .gitignore defeats all three by blanket-ignoring .aitools/. The gap is not in the rules — it is in the implementation.

proposals.what: Fix .gitignore to implement selective tracking within .aitools/ — gitignore ephemeral paths (scratch/, channel/session-*/) but explicitly un-ignore tracked paths (channel/running-estimate.json, channel/handoffs/). Use negation patterns: '!.aitools/channel/running-estimate.json', '!.aitools/channel/handoffs/'.
proposals.why: This is the root cause. Three rules agree on the correct behavior but .gitignore defeats them all. Until this is fixed, there is no working carry-forward location for running estimates. Every other proposal depends on this one.
proposals.barrier_analysis: LOW barrier. .gitignore negation patterns are well-understood git functionality. Risk: other concurrent sessions may also be modifying .gitignore (M4 is investigating concurrent sessions + channel architecture). Mitigation: coordinate with M4 findings before committing. The .gitignore change itself is simple, but the directory structure must exist for git to track the un-ignored files.

proposals.what: Add a PreToolUse hook on Write/Edit that detects when an agent writes carry-forward state (running-estimate.json, handoff-prompt.md, planning-brief.json) to .scratch/ and emits a warning via stderr: 'WARNING: [filename] is carry-forward state. Write to [canonical location] instead of scratch. Files in scratch are deleted at session end.' Detection via filename pattern matching.
proposals.why: Prevention layer. The /scratch skill's warning is in-context (agents may not have loaded it), but a hook fires at tool-use time regardless of context. This catches the mistake at write time rather than discovering it at session end. Addresses the gap where agents write to scratch because the canonical location does not work (P-1 must be fixed first, or the hook message must include the current workaround).
proposals.barrier_analysis: MEDIUM barrier. Requires: (1) a new hook script, (2) a filename pattern list of carry-forward artifacts, (3) testing that the hook does not false-positive on legitimately-named scratch files. The hook must be fail-open (never block a write, only warn). Edge case: what if an agent intentionally writes a temp copy of running-estimate.json to scratch for processing? The pattern match would trigger. Mitigation: only trigger on exact filenames, not partial matches.

proposals.what: Add a 'mock-session-lifecycle' verification type to tool-ops that tests harvest-session.sh end-to-end: creates a temp session dir with files of each classification (.json, .md, .py, .log, .tmp, commit-msg.txt), runs the hook, and verifies correct classification (harvested vs deleted), correct manifest entries (type, language), and correct cleanup (session dir removed).
proposals.why: The .json harvest path has never been tested in production (0 of 60 artifacts). The manifest entry would misclassify a running-estimate.json as type='code'. End-to-end lifecycle testing catches these issues before they surprise an agent or user. This also validates the stale-dir cleanup path in scratch-init.sh.
proposals.barrier_analysis: MEDIUM barrier. Requires: (1) test harness that creates realistic session dirs, (2) mock stdin for hook input, (3) assertions on harvesting/ contents and manifest state, (4) cleanup of test artifacts. The harvest-session.sh hook uses 'node -e' for manifest updates, so the test environment must have node available. Risk: test may interfere with real harvesting/ contents. Mitigation: use a temp directory as PROJECT_ROOT to isolate from real project state.

proposals.what: Add opportunistic harvesting to scratch-init.sh's stale-dir cleanup. Before rm-rf'ing a stale session dir, run the same classification logic from harvest-session.sh: copy non-ephemeral files to harvesting/ (if it exists), then delete. This closes the silent-data-loss path for crashed sessions.
proposals.why: Currently, if SessionEnd never fires (crash, kill, network loss), the next session's SessionStart silently destroys everything in the stale dir without any harvesting attempt. This is the ONLY deletion path that has no safety net. Even if carry-forward state should not be in scratch (P-1 and P-2 address that), artifacts like research docs and utility scripts would also be lost on crash.
proposals.barrier_analysis: HIGH barrier. Requires: (1) extracting the classification logic from harvest-session.sh into a shared function (currently inline), (2) making scratch-init.sh aware of harvesting/ location, (3) testing the interaction between stale cleanup and harvesting. Risk: scratch-init.sh runs at session START — if harvesting takes time, it delays session startup. Mitigation: only harvest files, skip manifest update (manifest update requires node and is slower). Alternative: just log a warning that stale dirs were found with non-ephemeral files, and let the user decide.

proposals.what: Update harvest-session.sh to recognize 'operational state' as a distinct artifact type alongside 'code' and 'ephemeral'. Files matching operational-state patterns (running-estimate.json, planning-brief.json) would be: (a) logged as a WARNING ('operational state found in scratch — should be in a permanent tracked location'), (b) harvested with type='operational-state' instead of type='code', and (c) given a longer prune window (90 days instead of 30) to increase the chance of manual recovery.
proposals.why: Even with P-1 and P-2, some agents will still write operational state to scratch (subagents that lack context, edge cases, user error). When this happens, the harvesting system should recognize the mistake and give the user a better chance to recover the data. Currently it would be silently classified as 'code' with generic metadata, making it hard to find during review.
proposals.barrier_analysis: LOW-MEDIUM barrier. Requires: (1) an operational-state filename pattern list in harvest-session.sh, (2) a new 'type' value in the manifest schema (currently only 'code'), (3) a warning log line. Risk: expanding the manifest schema requires updating the /harvest skill which governs that data. The filename pattern list must be maintained as new operational-state files are added. Mitigation: start with a small list (running-estimate.json, planning-brief.json) and expand incrementally.
